test: add ipykernel to the test group so the python3 kernel is registered in CI

Without ipykernel, NotebookClient (used by tests/test_tutorials.py and
by myst-nb at doc-build time) fails with

  jupyter_client.kernelspec.NoSuchKernel: No such kernel named python3

on a fresh CI venv. Locally ipykernel happens to be present via some
transitive install chain, but no installed package actually declares it
as a non-extra dependency, so a clean uv sync misses it.

Putting it in the test group covers both consumers — the test job
already installs the test group, and the docs-validate job does
`uv sync --group docs --group test`.

Enumerate termini per contiguous segment, not per chain

A chain is one run of residues only when every gap in it was modelled. Leave an
internal gap unmodelled and the builder receives two pieces with four ends
between them, but detectTermini offered the chain's outermost two -- so the two
ends the gap created were never put to the user, and the builder capped them by
its own default.

1LV1 is the case: an unmodelled GGSSG linker splits chain A, and the survey
handed over two termini for a structure that has four.

An end that exists because the residues beside it were never modelled is a cut
by construction, so `internal_gap` is decided before any reference evidence --
no UniProt mature-chain match can talk it into being natural. The chain's own
outermost ends keep their existing classification.
